outcome.technical: tools/reach-diff.py only. (1) HEAD IS BASE: after both sides are prepared, same_side() compares the content of the two sides. Two commits count as the same when they have the same sha or the same tree (a read-only rev-parse of each commit's tree). A WORKTREE head counts as the same when same_tree() finds its copy byte for byte equal to the base's export (files and symlinks; directories ignored). This changes no git state. When the sides are the same, no suite runs. The first line printed is 'reach-diff: the head is the base: no change to measure - <why>; no suite was run', and the exit is 2. The new --allow-same flag makes that exit 0 and still prints the line. Why this rule (also in the docstring, section THE HEAD IS THE BASE): 'lost: 0' over identical sides is true for every suite, so it measures nothing. A gate reads the exit code, not the text, so a line printed under an exit of 0 would still be a vacuous pass. Sides that differ anywhere are measured, so a task whose change the suite never reaches is an honest 0. A caller who expects identical sides (a re-run after the work was committed) says so with --allow-same. rd26 changed: --base HEAD --head HEAD used to expect exit 0 and now expects 2. (2) SOMETIMES-REACHED LINES: when any line looks lost, the base blocks that reached a lost line run once more, in a FRESH export of the base commit. Only those blocks run, and they are found per block: the hook's start marker now records its block, and read_traces returns by_block and silent_by_block. A lost line the recheck reaches again stays lost. A lost line the recheck misses, and any line only the recheck reached that the head misses, go under 'sometimes:' and result['flaky'] and do not affect the exit. The recheck refuses with 2 when it cannot rule out a non-random miss: a rechecked block failed, a trace could not be read, or a block left more silent processes or untraced module children than in its first run. I chose this over --base-runs N because it is on by default, costs nothing when nothing looks lost, and cannot set aside a line every base run reaches. The export is fresh because a rerun in the first run's export reads state that run left behind, and that state could hide a real loss; rd40 holds this and mutation M8 shows it. Limits, stated in the docstring: a line reached by chance in both base runs is still lost (flapping becomes rarer, not impossible), and the head is measured once. Other changes: reach_gaps also returns lost_at_base; _measure takes a work list and a pycache dir. New cases rd31-rd40; fixture tags race-base, race-marked, race-drop, race-fragile, race-hard, race-hard-drop, state-base, state-drop; rd39 uses a separate content-only worktree repo. Selftest ALL PASS 38/38. A real clean checkout (the driver tree) gives `--base HEAD --head WORKTREE` exit 2 in about 2.4 s (measured once), and its git status is empty before and after. DEPENDANTS: CONTRIBUTING.md (path) is still correct but now incomplete. Its usage line `--base <the commit before it> --head WORKTREE` is still right, and every refusal it lists still refuses. Its list of refusals does not name the two new ones (head is base; recheck could not confirm) or the 'sometimes:' list. I left it alone because it is outside this task's files; it is a candidate for a follow-up or the orchestrator's call. hook_line in tests/test__refs.py is that suite's own parameter name, not this module, so it is unaffected (test__refs 292 cases ok). parse_args/compare/main in close-phase.py, integrate-task.py, manage-worktrees.py, the .claude skills and the .claude hooks are other definitions with the same names, so they are unaffected.
outcome.descriptive: reach-diff refuses (exit 2, or 0 under --allow-same) when the head is the base instead of passing vacuously, and a line the base reaches only some of the time no longer makes a gate flap.
